Dynamic Corporate Transformation represents the enterprise as a dynamic system: an
evolving state $x(t) \in X$, governed by transformation operators, resourced by a
capital architecture, measured by a performance architecture, exposed through a risk,
resilience and robustness architecture, integrated into one unified architecture, and
steered by the General Enterprise Optimization Problem.

The map below is that sentence, drawn. It runs left to right in dependency order, from
the founding question to certified managerial action, over a rail of mathematical
prerequisites. Click any box to see what it depends on and what it feeds; the rest of
the map dims so the chain stands alone. Press *Play the seven moves* to walk the
sequence the course itself follows.

```{=html}
<div id="dct-map" data-dct-map="true" data-src="assets/dct-map/map.json"></div>
```

*Every box links to the chapter that develops it and to its AXIOM module. Boxes marked
as outline entries are placeholders whose commentary is still being written.*
